case_title: Kanhaiya Lal & Ors. v. State of Rajasthan
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the accused believed the deceased were responsible for the murder of the village leader's son, which led to revenge
weapon: Swords, gandasis (axe-like cutting weapons), sabals, sticks
evidence_type: Eyewitness (informant and relatives), medical evidence, recovery of weapons, site plan and autopsy
confession: None (weapons recovered on information given by accused in custody; not treated as a confession by the court)
aggravating_circumstances: Five deaths; ghastly and brutal assault in the house; High Court found the whole crime was committed in a planned design
mitigating_circumstances: Similarly placed persons given life sentence; accused in custody almost thirteen years; no specific overt acts attributed (High Court)
trial_court_outcome: Six accused sentenced to death (s.302); 11 accused sentenced to life imprisonment under s.302/149; the rest acquitted
high_court_outcome: Partly allowed: death sentences converted to life for several; some accused acquitted by benefit of doubt; convictions of Kanhaiyalal, Naval, Ram Lal and Radhey Shyam s/o Shankar Lal maintained
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 read with s.149 (for the accused whose convictions were maintained)
neutral_facts: On the evening of 28 June 2001, a group of about 25 to 30 persons from the village gathered outside the house where the victims were staying. They were armed with swords, gandasis, sabals and sticks. The group surrounded the house, climbed onto its roof and pelted stones, damaging the roof sheets and tiles. Several of the occupants escaped over a common wall into another room. Around midnight, the informant, his wife, his mother and another woman were made to sit on a neighbouring thatched roof. Shortly afterwards, a further group arrived in a jeep, broke open the door of the informant's house and inflicted blows with swords, gandasis and sticks. Three persons died inside the house. Two others were dragged outside and assaulted on the head, face, hands and feet with gandasis and swords, and both died. The attackers burnt two motorcycles belonging to the victims before leaving. The FIR was lodged at 6.45 a.m. on 29 June 2001. The informant explained that the family was too traumatised during the night to go to the police station. Investigators prepared a site plan, conducted autopsies, seized blood-stained clothing and recorded witness statements. Weapons were recovered on information given by accused persons in custody. The eyewitnesses were the informant and close relatives of the deceased. The defence contended that no independent witness was examined. The motive alleged was suspicion that the victims had killed the son of the village leader, which led to revenge.
physical_harm: Five deaths (Purshottam, Ram Kumar Dhaka, Kalu Lal Mali, Lakendra Sharma, Heera Lal Meghwal) from sword, gandasi and stick blows to head, face, hands and feet
number_of_offences: 7 charged; s.302 conviction finally upheld for the accused whose convictions were maintained (other sections not separately addressed in the Supreme Court judgment)
financial_property_loss: Two motorcycles taken and burnt (value not stated)
premeditation_planning: Found by the High Court and recorded in the judgment: the crime was committed in a planned design; the Supreme Court described it as revenge for suspected killing
motive: Revenge: the village Sarpanch suspected the deceased of killing his son (court accepted this motive)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of the informant and close relatives describing weapons, assault and injuries; medical corroboration; seized weapons; explained FIR delay
witness_credibility: Relatives scrutinised with care but found reliable and credible; testimony withstood cross-examination in material particulars; minor discrepancies only
custody_duration: Almost thirteen years (as stated by the Court)
trial_duration: offence: 28-29 June 2001; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 2 June 2005; Supreme Court: 22 April 2013
legal_representation: Accused: Sushil Kumar Jain, Puneet Jain, Anurag Gohil, Pratibha Jain. State: Imtiaz Ahmed, Naghma Imtiaz, Milind Kumar
investigation_status: FIR registered 29 June 2001 (6.45 a.m.); site plan, autopsy, seizures, statements, weapons recovered; charge-sheet filed and case committed to Sessions; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: 17 convicted (6 death, 11 life), rest acquitted. High Court: partly allowed; death converted to life for several; some acquitted; four convictions maintained. Supreme Court: all appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Not stated (the judgment records the State's counsel appearing but does not set out the State's submissions)
defence_argument: Delay in lodging FIR made the explanation unacceptable and the story embellished; relatives were interested witnesses and no independent witness was examined; witnesses did not specify each accused's role or weapon; innocent persons were implicated
legal_principle_applied: Delay in FIR is not fatal if adequately explained; relatives as witnesses scrutinised with care but not discarded merely for being related; appeal against acquittal interfered with only for compelling reasons; death penalty only in rarest of rare cases
precedent_relied_upon: State of H.P. v. Gian Chand (2001) 6 SCC 71; Ramdas v. State of Maharashtra (2007) 2 SCC 110; Meharaj Singh v. State of U.P. (1994) 5 SCC 188; Kilakkatha Parambath Sasi (AIR 2011 SC 1064); Hari Obula Reddy (1981) 3 SCC 675; Karlik Malhar (1996) 1 SCC 614; Masalti (AIR 1965 SC 202); Jadunath Singh (AIR 1972 SC 116); Sohrab (AIR 1972 SC 2020); Bacchudas (2007) 9 SCC 135; Shera Ram (2012) 1 SCC 602; Bachan Singh (1980) 2 SCC 684; Machhi Singh (1983) 3 SCC 470; Ram Pal (2003) 7 SCC 141
sentencing_rationale: Crime arose from suspicion-based revenge; similarly placed accused got life; long custody; not the rarest of rare case, so life imprisonment (commutation from death upheld)
judicial_mitigating_factors: No specific overt acts attributed to each accused; similarly placed accused given life; almost thirteen years in custody; Ram Narayan, who engineered the incident, died

case_title.quote: KANHAIYA LAL & ORS. v. STATE OF RAJASTHAN (Criminal Appeal No. 1108 of 2006)

number_of_accused.quote: conviction of 17 accused out of which six accused persons, namely, Yuvraj, Hemraj, Hansraj, Radhey Shyam, Modu Nath and Mohan

accused_gender.quote: though he was named along with other persons who constituted a group of 25-26 persons

victim_gender.quote: massacre of five persons, namely, Purshottam, Ram Kumar Dhaka, Kalu Lal Mali and Lakendra Sharma, all residents of village Railgaon, and Heera Lal Meghwal

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the father nurtured deep rooted suspicion that the deceased persons had not only masterminded a well thought out plan

offence_category.quote: Five persons of the same village were done to death by inflicting blows with swords, gandasis and sticks.

statutory_provisions.quote: all the accused persons were sent up for trial for offences punishable under Sections 147, 148, 302, 342, 427, 435 and 460 read with 149 IPC.

weapon.quote: came being armed with Gandasis, Swords, Sabals and sticks

evidence_type.quote: received corroboration from the evidence of the doctor. That apart, the weapons seized lends credence to the prosecution story.

confession.quote: on the basis of the information furnished by the accused persons, while they were in custody, recovered the weapons used in the commission of the crime

aggravating_circumstances.quote: Five people had been done to death.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: it is seen that similarly placed persons have been imposed life sentence. Quite apart from that, all the accused persons have almost spent thirteen years in custody.

trial_court_outcome.quote: the accused Mohan Lal, Yuvraj, Hansraj, Hemraj, Radhey Shyam s/o Gopal and Modu Nath were guilty of the offences under Sections 148, 427, 342, 460 and 302 IPC

high_court_outcome.quote: partly allowed the appeals preferred by Mohan Lal and others, who were convicted under Sections 302 and 460 IPC and sentenced to death

final_outcome.quote: the appeal filed by the accused-appellants and the appeals filed by the State for enhancement of penalty and reversal of the judgment of acquittal rendered in favour of the accused persons are dismissed.

offence_finally_established.quote: the conviction under Section 302 could not be interfered with.

imprisonment_type.quote: it cannot be said that imprisonment for life is inadequate and the circumstances are so grave that it calls for a death sentence

neutral_facts.quote: Purshottam, brother of the informant, Ram Kumar Dhakad, Kalu Lal Mali, Lakendra Sharma, and Heera Lal Meghwal had come on two motorcycles to the house of Purshottam

attempt_completion.quote: the real crime, the assault and the murder took place after midnight.

physical_harm.quote: assaulted them with Gandasis and swords on their heads, faces, hands and feet and, eventually, those two succumbed to their injuries.

number_of_offences.quote: all the accused persons were sent up for trial for offences punishable under Sections 147, 148, 302, 342, 427, 435 and 460 read with 149 IPC.

financial_property_loss.quote: They took both the motorcycles in the passage and burnt the same

premeditation_planning.quote: that the whole crime was committed in a planned design

motive.quote: the crime had taken place because Ram Narayan had suspected that the deceased persons were responsible for extinguishing the life spark of his son

key_evidence_accepted.quote: We find that their evidence is reliable and credible and it would not be inapposite not to act upon the same.

witness_credibility.quote: There is no earthly reason to categorise them as interested witnesses who would nurture an animus to see that the accused persons are convicted

custody_duration.quote: all the accused persons have almost spent thirteen years in custody.

trial_duration.quote: the intervening night of 28th and 29th June, 2001

legal_representation.quote: Sushil Kumar Jain, Puneet Jain, Anurag Gohil, Pratibha Jain for the Appellants. Imtiaz Ahmed, Naghma Imtiaz, Milind Kumar for the Respondent.

investigation_status.quote: submitted the charge-sheets on different dates before the Judicial Magistrate, Digod, who, in turn, committed the matter to the Court of Session.

appeal_history.quote: The Division Bench of the High Court partly allowed the appeals preferred by Mohan Lal and others

prosecution_argument.quote: Mr. Imtiaz Ahmed, learned counsel for the State in all the appeals.

defence_argument.quote: the prosecution version deserves to be thrown overboard inasmuch there is delay in lodging of the FIR

legal_principle_applied.quote: mere delay in lodging the First Information Report cannot be regarded by itself as fatal to the case of the prosecution

precedent_relied_upon.quote: In this regard, we may refer with profit a passage from State of H.P. v. Gian Chand

sentencing_rationale.quote: it is not a case which can be treated to be a case of extreme culpability and there is no other option but to impose death penalty.

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: when specific overt acts have not been attributed and similarly placed accused persons have been given life sentence

other_sentence_order.quote: Consequently, the appeal filed by the accused-appellants and the appeals filed by the State for enhancement of penalty and reversal of the judgment of acquittal rendered in favour of the accused persons are dismissed.
